text: Terraform's core engine knows nothing about Azure. A provider is the plugin that translates generic resource blocks into real API calls against one platform. For Azure, that plugin is azurerm.
A terraform block with required_providers names the provider's registry address and a version constraint. The provider block itself is required even when there's nothing to configure inside it.

A constraint like ~> 3.80 allows patch and minor updates but blocks the next breaking major version. Without a constraint, a teammate's unpinned init can silently resolve to a newer, incompatible provider release.
Running terraform init downloads the provider version matching your constraint and writes the exact resolved version into a lock file, committed to Git so everyone resolves to the same provider.
The provider is the translator between your HCL and Azure's API. Next up: the state file that tracks what that provider has actually built.
